title: The ground as a diffusive low-pass
question: Do the soil layers under Berlin damp and delay the daily and the annual temperature cycle as the heat equation predicts, with a damping depth √(ω_daily/ω_annual) ≈ 19 times larger for the annual cycle?

issues.text: The soil temperatures are ERA5-Land reanalysis, from a land-surface model that itself solves heat diffusion in four layers, not thermometers in the ground.
issues.fix: The plan tests the model's ground; the caveats say what a measured profile (a soil observatory) would add.

issues.text: Only one or two layers carry a measurable daily cycle, so the daily damping depth rests on the 0–7 and 7–28 cm layers.
issues.fix: The fit uses only layers whose amplitude is above 1% of the top layer's, and reports amplitude and phase estimates separately.

alternatives.question: Do amplitude and phase give the same damping depth for each cycle (as pure diffusion requires)?
alternatives.why: Drill down: a mismatch points to moisture, snow or layer-averaging effects.

alternatives.question: Is the damping depth different on sandy and clay soils (another place's soil type)?
alternatives.why: Expand: diffusivity depends on soil and water content.

hypotheses.statement: The log amplitude ratio falls linearly with depth for each cycle (exponential damping), with a slower decline for the annual cycle.
hypotheses.null: Amplitude does not depend on depth differently for the two cycles.

hypotheses.statement: The annual damping depth is about √365 ≈ 19 times the daily one (heat diffusion), not the same (a lumped lag).
hypotheses.null: The ratio of damping depths is far from 19 (outside 12–30).

concepts.label: Damping depth
concepts.description: d = √(2κ/ω): the depth over which a cycle's amplitude falls by e and its phase lags one radian.
concepts.why: The law's prediction is about it.

concepts.label: Thermal diffusivity
concepts.why: Both cycles should give the same κ.

concepts.label: Soil moisture
concepts.description: Water content per layer, which changes κ.

strategy.detail: Open-Meteo archive hourly soil_moisture_0_to_7cm … 100_to_255cm, same place and hours.

data.request: Hourly soil moisture for the same four ERA5 layers in Berlin, 2022–2024
data.why: Wet soil conducts heat better: split the fit by wet and dry seasons.

method.summary: For each cycle, ln(A/A_top) = −Δz/d and φ − φ_top = Δz/d, fitted through the origin over the layers above the noise; then d_annual/d_daily against √(ω_daily/ω_annual).

steps.title: Fetch three years of hourly air and soil temperature
steps.detail: Open-Meteo archive, Berlin, 2022–2024, four ERA5 soil layers.

steps.title: Fourier coefficients per layer
steps.detail: harmonics: amplitude_c and phase_rad at 24 h and 8766 h.

steps.title: Response relative to the top layer
Fit d per cycle
steps.detail: fit: d_amp_m, d_phase_m, kappa, annual_over_daily against sqrt_omega_law.

steps.title: Compare with √365
steps.detail: Accept or reject H2; repeat for a second place.

caveats: ERA5-Land soil temperature is model output on a ~9 km grid, not a measurement.
Layer temperatures are averages over thick layers (up to 1.55 m), so 'depth' is the layer middle.
Snow cover, freezing and soil moisture change κ through the year; the fit assumes one κ.
The surface energy balance (sun, evaporation) makes the top soil cycle differ from the air's; ratios are taken against the top soil layer for that reason.
